This PR was returned because of a verified blocking security issue: `GET /api/history` at `ledger/api.py:32` reads `account_id` without verifying ownership, violating requirement REQ-SEC-301 AC1. A probe verified that user `u-ben` was able to retrieve transfer records for account `acc-anna`.

Additionally, criterion AC1 has no automated acceptance test, and line `ledger/api.py:35` was never executed during testing. Performance under load, concurrency between simultaneous requests, and production configuration were not checked.

In `ledger/money.py:8`, `to_cents` was changed to parse amounts using `float` instead of `Decimal`. Because floats cannot represent every cent value accurately, the invariant `parse_is_exact` failed: `to_cents('19985.01')` returned `1998500` instead of `1998501`. This introduces precision errors into callers like `POST /api/transfer` and `GET /api/fee`. 

Additionally, changed line `ledger/money.py:22` was not checked by execution in any test. Performance under load, concurrency between simultaneous requests, and production configuration were also not checked.

This PR is blocked because it violates requirement REQ-OBS-401 AC3 by exposing unmasked PII. In `ledger/transfers.py:22`, `log.warning` writes the raw `to_iban` to logs instead of using `mask_iban()`. This presents a one-way merge danger because sensitive data written to log storage cannot be retracted once live.

Additionally, changed line `ledger/transfers.py:46` was not checked by test execution. Performance under load, concurrency between simultaneous requests, and production configuration were also not checked.

Merging this causes immediate query failures and irreversible data loss:

1. Acceptance test `REQ_DATA_502.test_ac1_csv_has_memo` regressed with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: memo`.
2. `ledger/statements.py:7` breaks because it still reads the dropped column (`SELECT created_day, to_iban, amount_cents, fee_cents, memo FROM transfers...`).
3. Running `migrations/002_drop_memo.sql:1` permanently destroys stored `memo` data; reverting the code will not restore it.

Additionally, the changed line at `ledger/transfers.py:51` was not checked by any test execution. AC1 has no acceptance test, and performance under load, concurrency between simultaneous requests, and production configuration were plainly not checked.

No. Differential testing showed that `transfer_fee` at `ledger/fees.py:12` changes behavior: 39 of 4,000 random inputs differ. For example, `transfer_fee(57250, 'instant')` was 115 on base, but is now 114. 

Additionally, module-level definitions changed at `ledger/fees.py:6`, and changed lines `ledger/fees.py:16` and `ledger/fees.py:17` were never checked by test execution. AC4 (half-up rounding) was not checked because no acceptance test exists.

The tests caught a regression on acceptance criterion AC2 ("Pending transfers count toward the daily limit"). Test `REQ_PAY_210.test_ac2_pending_counts` passed on main but failed on this PR because `TransferError` was not raised.

This regression stems from `ledger/transfers.py:16`, which modified the query to only count `status = 'booked'`, omitting pending transfers from the daily total.

Across the suite, 20 spec tests ran: 12 passed, 7 were already failing, and 1 regressed. Note that changed line `ledger/transfers.py:18` was never executed by any test. UI tests, concurrency, and performance under load were not checked.

The PR caused a regression in acceptance test `REQ_UI_601.test_ac1_fee_updates`, which passed on `main` but failed on this PR. The test evidence shows `#fee shows "€0.00", expected "€0.50"`. 

In `web/app.js:30`, the code replaces `$("kind").addEventListener("change", refreshFee);` with `$("kind").addEventListener("change", (e) => localStorage.setItem(KIND_KEY, e.target.value));`. Because `refreshFee` is no longer called when the transfer kind changes, the displayed fee does not update.

Only AC1 ("Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the original transfer and debits once") is tested, verified by `REQ_PAY_230.test_ac1_retry_debits_once`.

AC2 ("Idempotency keys are scoped to the user who sent them") has no acceptance test and was not checked. In `ledger/transfers.py:25`, the helper dropped the `user_id = ?` filter from the lookup, but the AI could not verify if this change meets AC2. Concurrency, load performance, and production configuration were also not checked.

No. AC4 (“Fees round half-up to the cent”) is not covered by any test.

The PR context marks AC4’s status as “no test” and explicitly notes that the product owner supplied no acceptance test for it. Consequently, AC4 was not checked. The AI flagged an open question for @aino.payments to confirm AC4 manually or add an acceptance test, refusing to vouch for it from code inspection alone, even though `ledger/fees.py:12` includes `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`.

In total, 3 files are affected across the codebase. Broader runtime impacts—specifically performance under load, concurrency between simultaneous requests, and production configuration—were not checked.

No. A code revert cannot safely roll this back. This change is classified as a one-way door because `migrations/002_drop_memo.sql:1` permanently destroys stored data in the `transfers` table, which a code revert does not restore. 

Additionally, the column is still actively needed: `ledger/statements.py:7` still queries `memo`, causing a verified regression where `REQ_DATA_502.test_ac1_csv_has_memo` fails with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: memo`.

Whether this data has been backed up or confirmed unneeded was not checked and is flagged as an open question for @sara.data. Concurrency, production configuration, and performance under load were also not checked.

In `ledger/fees.py:6`, the PR defines a cap of 500 cents (`INSTANT_MAX_CENTS = 500`).

In `ledger/fees.py:16`, it modifies `transfer_fee` to clamp instant transfer fees between the existing minimum and the new cap: `return min(max(int(fee), INSTANT_MIN_CENTS), INSTANT_MAX_CENTS)`.

This ensures instant transfer fees do not exceed EUR 5.00, satisfying acceptance criterion AC3. Acceptance test `REQ_PAY_204.test_ac3_instant_cap` now passes. Note that AC4 (half-up rounding) was not checked because no acceptance test was supplied.

At `ledger/transfers.py:25`, the query dropped `AND user_id = ?` and now looks up transfers solely using `WHERE idempotency_key = ?`. 

The risk is that idempotency keys are no longer scoped to the specific user making the transfer. If a user submits an idempotency key previously used by someone else, this query can return another user's transfer. This directly impacts requirement AC2 ("Idempotency keys are scoped to the user who sent them"). Whether this scope change was intended was not checked by the AI, and AC2 was not verified because no acceptance test was provided.

In `ledger/fees.py:12`, differential testing found that for an instant transfer of 57,250 cents (`transfer_fee(57250, 'instant')`), the fee was previously 115 cents, but now returns 114 cents. Across 4,000 random inputs, 39 produced different results following the table change in `ledger/fees.py:8`.

According to the PR description and the added comment at `ledger/transfers.py:13`, the agent changed the query to speed it up by reading only settled (`booked`) transfers so the database could use a `(from_account, status)` index.

However, changing the query at `ledger/transfers.py:16` to exclude `pending` transfers caused the acceptance test `REQ_PAY_210.test_ac2_pending_counts` to fail, violating requirement AC2 ("Pending transfers count toward the daily limit").

Additionally, performance under load was not checked, and changed line `ledger/transfers.py:18` was not checked by execution in any test.

The agent needs to fix the regression in REQ-UI-601 (`REQ_UI_601.test_ac1_fee_updates`), where `#fee` shows "€0.00" instead of the expected "€0.50". 

In `web/app.js:29`, the agent replaced `refreshFee` on the `"change"` event listener with `(e) => localStorage.setItem(KIND_KEY, e.target.value)`. As a result, changing the transfer kind no longer recalculates the fee. The agent must ensure `refreshFee` continues to run when the selection changes, in addition to storing the chosen value in `localStorage`.

In `ledger/api.py:33-34`, `get_metrics(db, user_id, params)` directly returns `metrics.snapshot()` with no permission checks inside the function body. 

Furthermore, `ledger/api.py:34` was never executed in any test. Whether framework-level routing provides authentication or authorization was not checked. The AI flagged `ledger/api.py:33` as an open security question, asking who is allowed to call `GET /api/metrics` and whether everything it returns is safe for them to see.
